title: Developer first-experience flowcards: auth, streaming handshake, and tool-call sequences
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Produce a compact set of high-fidelity "flowcards" (small, self-contained visual assets) for the API/SDK quickstart docs that explain: 1) API key onboarding and rotation, 2) streaming handshake and SSE vs WebSocket behavior, 3) tool-calling lifecycle (request, function signature, tool execution, response), and 4) error/fallback surfaces for private/dedicated fallbacks. These assets will be used in: the SDK quickstart page, the 'first call' modal in the Console, and a short 'copyable' markdown pack for the docs repo.

Scope: 6 distinct flowcards + 3 device-size variations (desktop preview, mobile banner, inline doc tile). Each asset must have annotated layers so engineers can extract code snippets and copy alt text for accessibility. Include two screenshot-ready product captures demonstrating: a successful streaming session and a tool-call with metadata headers shown.

Non-goals: Full page onboarding microcopy updates (PM will coordinate separately), redesign of existing Console welcome modal, multi-language localization (will be a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Six flowcards exported as SVG and PNG (light/dark) with annotated layers in a Figma file - filenames prefixed with ss-flowcard-
Each flowcard has a compact (280x160) and full (880x420) layout, and an accessible alt-text string provided
Two screenshot assets captured from Console staging showing streaming session and tool-call; image files uploaded to Drive with links
A short markdown pack (README.md) with copy + 3 code snippets for JS SDK: auth example, streaming handshake, and tool call example
Design tokens documented (colors, spacing, iconography) so engineering can implement pixel-accurate embeds
Security review signoff for any asset that surfaces key rotation UX language
Design handoff completed (Figma link + layer-export instructions) and a linked GitHub PR created to add assets to docs repo
comments: 2026-03-05 Maya Chen: Initial spec and asset list posted. Decided to prioritize compact flowcards for the docs header and a separate full-size for the Console modal. Asked Eng for signal on header propagation for streaming UI.

2026-03-06 Liam O'Rourke: Sketched low-fidelity flows in Figma: 1) key create -> store -> rotate, 2) stream handshake (client->server->ACK->events), 3) toolcall (prompt -> function schema -> tool exec -> enriched response). Added initial frame names and layer conventions.
2026-03-06 Nora Patel (PM): Confirmed scope and asked to include a brief alt-text that mentions 'no secrets in images' and to avoid showing full API keys in screenshots. Marked for security review.

2026-03-07 Security (Ravi S.): Flagged wording in the key-rotation card that implied key sharing; requested updated copy: 'rotate keys regularly; do not embed keys in client-side code' and approval before export.

2026-03-07 Alex G. (Engineering): Noted streaming handshake card must show both SSE and WebSocket variants; asked for a micro-callout about reconnect/backoff behavior and KV cache warm start (one-liner).

2026-03-08 Maya Chen: High-fidelity frames uploaded to Figma; exported a draft PNG set and attached to Drive. Requested design review with PM and Eng next Monday. Added layer notes for code-snippet extraction.
2026-03-08 Liam O'Rourke: Implemented contrast tweaks for dark-mode assets and added explicit alt-text strings in the Figma file. Preparing the markdown pack and test code snippets for JS SDK.
2026-03-08 Nora Patel (PM): Approved layout choices. Assigned follow-up to PM-4127 for localization planning after this release.
notes: Prefer using schematic icons (lined) rather than product UI for generic flowcards to reduce support overhead. Product screenshots reserved for Console-specific tiles only.
implementation_tips: Export SVG with separate groups for 'code', 'sequence', and 'annotations' so the docs build can selectively show/hide code snippets. Include a short CSS snippet in the README showing how to embed the 280x160 variant inline with proper padding.
qa_checklist: 1) Verify alt text for each asset; 2) Validate no API keys in images; 3) Confirm screenshot timestamps and staging URLs are ephemeral; 4) Confirm PR merges before release branch cut
